text: If the client has thin finance-process evidence today, what should AbarVa say and ask for next?
claudePromptBoundary: Full production prompt is reconstructed from current source template and captured source packet. ai_egress_audit stores prompt hash/snapshot refs, not raw prompt text by default.
claudeResponse:
Lakeshore Holdings has more loaded evidence than the question implies — but the framing is right in one important way: what's loaded is strong on Legal Ops baselines and Treasury/Finance system context, and thinner on the actual finance-process volumes, cycle times, and unit costs that would make any Value Office claim Finance-attestable.
Here's what AbarVa should say directly to the CIO or CFO: "We have enough to start, but not enough to make board-grade claims yet. The loaded evidence shows your systems, your AI initiatives, and your Legal Ops queue baselines.
" The specific asks should be: (1) Finance close baseline — current period-end close duration by entity, reconciliation aging, and number of open items at day-10 post-close. This is the treasury/finance equivalent of the 780-item Legal queue that's already loaded.
(2) Exception and rework cost — payment exception volumes out of Kyriba, SAP mapping defect counts, and any SOX control-failure frequency. Without this, the Treasury lighthouse use case stays directional. (3) A named Finance-process owner — someone with authority to attest the baseline and co-own the KPI target.
The Legal Ops owner role is already established in the loaded evidence; Finance needs the same. (4) Semantic layer readiness — confirmation that GL and cost-center definitions in Oracle Fusion and BlackLine are clean enough to support automated reporting.
The 68 data sources already flagged in the loaded evidence signal manual workarounds; Finance needs to confirm which sources are authoritative. What AbarVa should not do is fabricate a savings estimate or inflate the pilot target.
The loaded context is explicit: Finance already reduced the initial value assumption to 8-12% cycle-time improvement for the pilot, and outside-counsel avoidance is directional only. That discipline applies equally to Finance process claims.
The right posture is: lead with what's proven (Legal Ops queue, Treasury system map, ERP controls program), name exactly what's missing, and offer the CIO a clear choice — authorize planning assumptions so the roadmap can move, or provide the four data inputs above so the baseline is Finance-attested before any board paper is written.
--- Finance-Process Evidence Status | Evidence area | What's loaded | What's missing | Decision implication |
|---|---|---|---|
| Treasury / Kyriba | System named; cash visibility program active | Payment exception volumes; SOX attestation; bank certification evidence | Can't size Treasury lighthouse without exception-cost baseline |
| Finance close / ERP | Oracle Fusion + ERP controls modernization program loaded | Close cycle time by entity; reconciliation aging; open-item counts | Can't set a Finance-attested KPI target without close baseline |
| GL semantic layer | 68 data sources flagged; MuleSoft integration hub named | Authoritative source confirmation; lineage certification | Automated reporting risk until semantic owner is named |
| Finance process owner | CFO role implied in discipline note | Named owner with baseline sign-off authority | Board-grade claims require an attesting owner, not just a system owner |
| Value assumption | Finance reduced pilot target to 8-12% cycle-time improvement | Hard savings evidence for outside-counsel avoidance and exception cost | Planning assumptions allowed only with CIO/CFO authorization |
